title: Marian O'Connell: Artist Books and Etchings
description: Marian O'Connell's exquisite intaglio prints are inspired by things she loves: New England flowers, gardens and architecture. O'Connell's hand-painted accordion book Walls, Gates and Fences, 2008 won "Best in Show" and the "Newport Art Museum Award" in the 2009 Newport Annual Members' Juried Exhibition. Museum members free; non-members $10 suggested donation.

title: William Klenk: Collage Paintings
description: William Klenk's painterly collages have a transformative power that "connects us to our world in a different way than painting does. Collage uses actual material from our lives - bits of signs, posters and letters - and combines them in a way that transforms the elements into something else." Klenk has taught drawing and painting at the University of Rhode Island for five decades.

title: Newport Cooks! The Mysteries of Baking Revealed
description: Taught by Chef Karen Benjamin, The Creative Cake Company. Come to one class or take all three and you too can unravel the many mysteries of baking. $50 per class. Class I: Cakes with the Expert – February 17th. Class II: Pastry & Crusts – February 24th. Class III: Custards – March 3rd.

title: Jamestown: A History of Narragansett Bay’s Island Town
description: Rosemary Enright and Sue Maden, authors of the new book "Jamestown:, will discuss how Jamestown’s history has been shaped by its geography. Jamestown was part of the larger world when merchants and travelers used the common roadway of the bay. As the speed of transportation on land increased, that same bay isolated the town. Enright and Maden will share how the island developed into the community it is today. $5 per person, Reservations requested.

title: Music Series at Trinity: Matthew Truss and Brent Erstad
description: This opening program will feature American countertenor Matthew Truss and pianist Brent Erstad in an evening of French Melodies and American Spirituals. Mr. Truss has garnered international acclaim both on the concert and opera stage. Praised for his “mellifluous voice and ebullient manner,” he is making his mark as a young performer whose “precocious voice boasts both beauty and volume.”

title: Newport Cooks! Laissez Les Bon Temps Rouler: Cajun, Creole & Louisiana Cookin’ on Mardi Gras
description: The good times will be rolling in this cooking class as we celebrate Mardi Gras with Private Chefs Sophia Pendergast & Miles Chandler of Saucery. Their love of New Orleans spills over into their extensive culinary knowledge of Cajun, Creole & local cuisine. Open any Louisiana cookbook and you’ll see, “first you make a roux”. In class you’ll make a roux as we learn to prepare Crawfish Etouffee & other flavorful & spicy delights. Wine tasting to compliment the meal. Class fee: $50

title: Newport Cooks! Modern Local Fresh on The Ides of March
description: Taught by Food & Wine Magazine nominated Best Chef of the Year Jake Rojas. With a main course of pork, you’ll be certain it is local & prepared with an artist’s eye for detail. Chef Jake will share valuable tips for sourcing the best ingredients & kitchen secrets for prepping & preparing a 3-course meal like you might eat at delightful Tallulah on Thames.  Even seasoned cooks will take home nuggets of gold from this bright and talented Chef!  Wine tasting to compliment the meal. Class fee:$50

title: An Affinity with Newport: The 18th Century Architecture of Marblehead, MA
description: Historian Judy Anderson will discuss the colonial architectural heritage of Marblehead, MA which shares much in common with Newport, RI. Hundreds of pre-Revolutionary War homes line the streets of both communities. She will focus on the colonial architecture of Marblehead, placing it in context with the town’s colonial-era history & discuss conditions for construction, survival & preservation. $5 per person. A joint program between Newport Historical Society & Newport Restoration Foundation.

title: A Night of Irish Music with Robbie O’Connell
description: Robbie O’Connell, a Clancy family Irish folk performer, will grace the mansion parlors with an intimate performance on at 7:30pm. Within recent years, Robbie O’Connell  has performed solo throughout the East Coast as well as in Ireland. Tickets are $20, $15 for Linden Place Members, free for Colt Circle members and includes a wine reception to meet the performer.  Reservations are recommended.

title: Estate Gardeners of Newport: Putting a Human Face on Newport’s Horticultural History
description: Harry Eudenbach, author of "Estate Gardeners of Newport: A Horticultural Legacy", will highlight how Newport’s rich Colonial history set the stage for two centuries of horticultural pursuits by well-to-do Aquidneck Island estate owners. He will focus on the individual gardeners who cared for and nurtured Newport’s renowned gardens and landscapes. Reservations requested. $5 per person

title: Journey: Recent Work by Rugmaker Meg Little
description: Meg Little uses historical techniques and durable modern materials to create her striking, abstract hand-tufted rugs. Cultural artifacts from around the world and contemporary art by artists such as David Hockney inspire Little's designs. She uses a basic design vocabulary - stripe, spot, circle, cross, spiral. These shapes mirror the simplest hand gestures and have been used for decorative purposes since pre-historic times.

title: Choral Evensong for the 1st Sunday of Lent
description: The Ecclesia Consort will present a Lenten Choral Evensong at 4pm with a reception following. Lent is a wonderful time of reflection and the opportunity to hear Ecclesia sing beautiful renaissance polyphony entirely a cappella; works of Victoria, Conseil, Palestrina, Farrant and Gregorian Chant in Emmanuel's beautiful nave. The service is open to all and a freewill offering will be received. Free Parking is available in the church's own parking lot.

title: Gardens of Paris - A personal "Tour" with Maureen Bovet

Drawing on her experience as a tour guide for the Paris Garden Guild (2001-2004), Bovet will take you from well-known historic parks.

title: Tour the Wanton-Lyman-Hazard House with Polly Wanton Lyman

Polly will take guests through the house’s parlor, keeping room, kitchen & bed chambers while telling stories of the house’s great history & discussing life in Revolutionary War-torn Newport. Guests will have the opportunity to talk to Polly & ask questions about her daily life. Reservations suggested for this 11am tour. $10 per person.

title: Patronesses on the Point: A Walking Tour of Women and Newport Architecture

Some built fanciful farms, while other explored cutting-edge architectural styles, such as Shingle Style. $12 per person, $10 for Newport Historical Society members.
